note: CRITICAL ORDERING: revokeGrant must be sub-call index 0, release must be sub-call index 1. Both execute within the same Ethereum transaction — same block, same block.timestamp.

execution_mechanism.instruction: In Safe UI: New Transaction → Transaction Builder → add sub-call 0 (revokeGrant) → add sub-call 1 (release) → Create Batch → Execute
execution_mechanism.why_same_block: Safe executes the batch as a single execTransaction call, which delegates to MultiSend. All sub-calls occur within one Ethereum tx and share block.timestamp.

effective_time_analysis.condition: _effectiveTime: g.revoked && queryTime > g.revokedAt → T > T → FALSE
effective_time_analysis.result: _effectiveTime returns T (cap does NOT apply — strict > boundary)
effective_time_analysis.conclusion: release() computes the same vested amount as revokeGrant() — same formula, same inputs

GrantRevoked_event.claimable: vested_at_T (all vested is claimable since released==0)

expected_outcome.release_effect: release() succeeds: reads g.revoked=true (A2), _effectiveTime returns T (not capped), vestedAmount=vested_at_T, unreleased=vested_at_T-0=vested_at_T>0. Mints vested_at_T tokens.
expected_outcome.post_tx_formula_freeze: vestedAmount(beneficiary) in any later block = floor(1000 * (revokedAt - 1759547342) / 31536000) = vested_at_T
expected_outcome.post_tx_nothing_to_release: release(beneficiary) in any later block: g.released=vested_at_T, vestedAmount=vested_at_T, unreleased=0 → reverts NothingToRelease

failure_condition.if_release_reverts: release() in same-tx reverted — would indicate _effectiveTime applied the cap when queryTime==revokedAt (unexpected strictness behavior), or g.revoked not yet visible (A2 violation)
failure_condition.numeric_contradiction: If release() reverts with NothingToRelease in same tx: unreleased=0 means vested_at_T was 0 at query time — contradicts revokeGrant emitting vested_at_T>0 moments earlier in same block
